t: Warmington calls Ayotte's budget-based moratorium too slow
b: Both candidates for governor favor freezing new data center permits. Ayotte says she opposes the Bow and Nottingham proposals; Warmington argues a pause in next year's budget could come after a big project lands.

t: Westfield denies a permit extension for the Servistar hyperscale campus
b: The unanimous vote lets the 2021 special permit lapse at the end of October, likely ending what would have been New England's largest data center. Servistar never bought the land; it has 20 days to appeal.

t: Bucksport adopts a six-month data center moratorium
b: The 5–2 vote covers all data centers, not just large ones. At least two data center firms have eyed the mostly vacant former Verso paper mill, though none has applied.

t: Over 100 rally in Bow against a data center at Merrimack Station
b: Residents protested outside a select board meeting over a possible hyperscale project at the shuttered coal plant, citing water, noise and property values. No application has been filed.

t: New Haven adopts a 12-month data center moratorium
b: Alders present voted unanimously, with an exception for quantum computing. Without the pause, data centers would be allowed as of right in industrial zones and the Union Station area.

t: Senate Republicans back Ayotte and pledge data center legislation
b: Carson said the caucus agrees with the governor on halting data center construction and will pursue a bill to keep the costs off taxpayers. She gave no timeline.
iw: Both parties now favor a pause

t: Nottingham voters approve a 12-month data center moratorium, 1,335 to 143
b: The special election followed a warehouse-conversion proposal withdrawn amid backlash. The planning board is drafting zoning that could ban data centers permanently.

t: Regulators order Rhode Island Energy to propose a tariff for 20 MW-plus loads
b: The rate case ruling requires a filing by Dec. 31 meant to keep data centers and other very large loads from shifting costs, straining reliability or causing rate shock. Legislative cost bills had stalled.

t: FERC orders ISO New England to justify or rewrite its large-load rules
b: The show cause order preliminarily finds ISO-NE's tariff may be unjust because it lacks provisions for studying, connecting and charging data centers and other big loads, including co-located ones.
iw: New England grid rules in flux

t: SB 439 dies after amendments to make data centers allowed by right
b: Democrats proposed it to give towns tools to regulate data centers. Republican changes would have required towns to allow them in commercial and industrial zones, and the bill died at adjournment.

t: Maine bars new data centers from key business tax breaks
b: LD 713 makes data centers that start operating after July ineligible for the business equipment tax exemption and the Dirigo program. The state must study other incentives and report by Nov. 4.

t: Canterbury voters change zoning to ban data centers
b: The March town meeting acted with no project proposed, one of several New England towns moving preemptively.

t: House kills a bill creating New Hampshire's first data center incentives
b: HB 1739 would have offered property tax deals and business tax credits, conditioned on paying grid costs and joining demand response. It was found inexpedient to legislate on a voice vote.

t: Energy affordability bill in conference could add data center rules
b: The House version would create a data center-specific tariff; the Senate's largely writes in Healey's expectations on clean power, water and community benefits. Negotiators were reconciling them in September.

t: Wiscasset pauses talks on a $5 billion data center on town land
b: The select board halted discussions after resident pushback and is drafting a review process with no set end date. The plan also cost the town a $240,000 county housing award for the same land.
iw: Indefinite halt to a major proposal

t: LiquidCool plans Maine's first large AI data center at the former Loring base
b: The Limestone project would fill an existing warehouse, with a Versant deal for 24 MW on top of 2 MW already in the building. The company says its immersion cooling avoids water use.

t: Consent order lets Markley install disputed generators while the appeal is pending
b: Residents learned of the order only in January 2026. Their lawsuit says it exceeded MassDEP's authority, and in August 2026 a judge stayed the permit.
iw: Construction allowed before a final permit

t: Residents organize after a $5 billion data center plan surfaces in Wiscasset
b: The plan for town-owned land along the Back River became public in mid-September. Neighbors formed Protect Wiscasset, saying little was disclosed about the end user, power source or grid impacts.

t: Tax break revives a Westfield hyperscale plan worth up to $4 billion
b: At a state hearing on the exemption's rules, Westmass called the incentive critical to Servistar's 10- to 14-building plan. The Conservation Law Foundation urged stronger energy, water and efficiency safeguards.

t: New Hampshire lets off-grid power plants sell directly to big users
b: HB 672 exempts generators that never connect to the grid from utility regulation and renewable standards, a path for data centers to bring their own power. Siting, zoning and environmental permits still apply.

t: Lowell neighbors' appeal of the data center's air permit is turned away
b: A hearing officer found seven of the eight residents lacked standing and in December recommended upholding the permit, which the commissioner later did. The residents then took the case to Superior Court.

t: MassDEP approves eight more diesel generators at Lowell's Markley data center
b: The air plan brings the site to 27 generators and 16 cooling towers, some within 100 feet of homes. Opponents say it was approved without a cumulative impact analysis or state environmental review.

t: Bloomfield commissioners balk at a data center near Bradley airport
b: Members raised noise, building height, airport proximity and lost open space when the proposal came up in June 2025. A year later it still had not been approved.

t: Maine law caps data centers' share of on-site power at a Millinocket mill
b: Emergency law LD 912 strips a generator's utility exemption if more than 25% of its capacity serves data centers. It targets the former Great Northern mill site, keeping its on-site hydropower available to other employers.
iw: Limits data center access to cheap hydropower

t: Rhode Island's 30-year data center tax break bills are held for study
b: S0921 and H6097 offered sales and property tax relief for $200 million investments in enterprise or opportunity zones, $400 million elsewhere. The tax administrator flagged weak job requirements; similar 2026 bills also stalled.

t: Waterford lets NE Edge hand its Millstone data center deal to a subsidiary
b: The 2–1 vote kept alive a 2023 host agreement worth $231 million over 30 years, with building permits due by March 2026. The Siting Council had rejected a key petition in 2024; a project database now lists the deal as terminated.

t: Bill to repeal towns' temporary moratorium power fails
b: SB 163 would have repealed RSA 674:23, the law towns use to adopt temporary building moratoriums. Its defeat left that authority in place as data center fights reached New Hampshire towns.

t: Massachusetts creates a 20-year sales tax exemption for large data centers
b: The Mass Leads Act covers equipment, software, electricity and construction for sites of at least 100,000 sq ft, $50 million and 100 jobs. Certification rules went to a hearing in August 2025; Healey paused applications in June 2026.

t: Wallingford rezones to allow data centers in its Watershed Interchange District
b: The town, which has its own electric utility, opened the district to data centers as other Connecticut towns moved to restrict them.

t: Groton caps data centers at 12,500 square feet, shutting out hyperscale projects
b: Adopted after a 2022 moratorium, the rules also bar water cooling. A developer sued for more than $5 billion, and towns as far away as Georgia now cite the rules as a model.
